title: MRI for children with sedation
what: An MRI during which your child sleeps with medicine. This way your child lies still and is not scared of the noise.
why: For young children and children who cannot lie still for 20 to 40 minutes.
duration: the MRI itself usually takes 20 to 60 minutes; with prep and waking up, 2 to 4 hours
tell_doctor: Your child's long-term illnesses, allergies, and medicines
If your child recently had a runny nose, cough, or fever. Sedation may be postponed
If your child or relatives had problems with anesthesia
Metal and implants in the body, such as a cochlear implant

prepare.title: Fasting
prepare.text: Before sedation, your child cannot eat or drink for a set time. Usually: food 6 hours before, breast milk 4 hours, clear water 2 hours. The anesthesiologist will tell you the exact times.

prepare.title: Checkup
prepare.text: A pediatrician checkup and tests are often needed. Ask the clinic for the list.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: Clothes with no metal: no snaps, zippers, or rhinestones.

prepare.title: Toy
prepare.text: A favorite toy and a bottle of water for after waking up.

bring: The pediatrician's report and tests, if asked
Diapers, a change of clothes, and water
steps: The anesthesiologist checks your child and asks you about their health
An IV line is put in a vein. Sometimes a mask with medicine is used first
Your child falls asleep while you watch
Your child is placed in the scanner, and the anesthesiologist watches breathing and pulse
You wait nearby, outside the room
After the scan, your child is woken up and brought to you
feel: It does not hurt your child
After waking, your child may be sleepy, fussy, or cry. This passes
after: Your child rests under observation, usually for 30 to 60 minutes
Your child can eat and drink when the doctor allows. Usually start with water
For the rest of the day, keep things calm, with an adult nearby
The report usually comes in 1 to 3 days
red_flags: Your child does not wake up, breathes poorly, or has blue lips: call emergency services right away
Repeated vomiting or a high fever after sedation: call your doctor or emergency services

faq.q: Is sedation dangerous for my child?
faq.a: It is given by an anesthesiologist, who watches your child the whole time. Serious problems are rare.

faq.q: Can I be with my child while they fall asleep?

faq.a: An empty stomach protects against food getting into the airways during sleep.

reminders.text: Your child's MRI with sedation is tomorrow. Check the time after which your child cannot eat or drink.
